name: Hydrangea
grown_as: A compact ornamental shrub, William's is 'Euphoria Pink'. The wild species and most of its varieties carry flat lacecap heads, which the description follows; some newer varieties carry rounder heads with double florets. Colour depends on the soil: pink in neutral or limy soil, blue in acid soil. ⚠️ CHECK whether 'Euphoria Pink' has lacecap or round heads
habit: A compact, rounded deciduous shrub, 0.8 to 1.2 m, with many upright, unbranched stems from the base.

leaf.outline: Lance-shaped to narrowly oval, 5 to 12 cm long, narrower and thinner than the common big-leaved hydrangea
leaf.tip: Drawn out to a long point
leaf.margin: Sharp, regular teeth like a saw (hence serrata) from about a third of the way up to the tip; the base untoothed
leaf.veins: A midrib and six to eight pairs of side veins curving forward, pressed in
leaf.surface: Matt, slightly rough mid green above; paler beneath with hairs on the veins
leaf.colour: Mid green, often reddening in autumn

flower.form: A flat-topped lacecap head: a dome of tiny fertile flowers in the middle, ringed by a few large showy florets
flower.petals: Each showy outer floret has three to five (usually four) broad, petal-like sepals, rounded or toothed at the tip; the tiny inner flowers have five minute petals
flower.colour: Pink (blue in acid soil); the centre a deeper pink, the outer florets paler
flower.centre: Many tiny fertile flowers like beads, opening into a fuzz of stamens
flower.behind: Nothing showing; the head sits on branched stalks
flower.carried: One head at the tip of each stem, held flat and upright
flower.size: Head 6 to 10 cm across; outer florets 2 to 3 cm
flower.season: July to September; the heads dry papery and red-green with age and stay on through winter

fruit: Tiny dry capsules in the old heads; the dried outer florets stay round them.
seedling: Not drawn: grown as bought plants
winter: Bare upright stems with fat paired buds near the top; the dry, papery, brown flower heads left on as frost protection.

leaf: simple lance-shaped leaf with a long pointed tip
sharp saw teeth on the upper two-thirds, none at the base
bloom: a flat head of tiny bead-like flowers in the centre
a ring of larger florets round it, each of four broad petal-like sepals
young: several upright stems from the base
pointed toothed leaves in opposite pairs
dormant: bare upright stems with paired buds
dry papery brown flower heads left on top
flower: a flat pink lacecap head on top of each stem
growing: a rounded bush of upright stems
opposite pointed leaves, no flowers yet

look_alikes: Big-leaved hydrangea (Hydrangea macrophylla) has larger, broader, glossier leaves and usually round mophead heads. Viburnum lacecaps (such as guelder rose) are white, with lobed or rounded leaves and red berries. Climbing hydrangea has white lacecaps and climbs by roots.
